programme_name: Cross-lineage portability of plant trait phylogenetic memory

relationship_to_prior_work.rule: The failed variance-ratio question is not relaxed. This follow-up asks whether trait identity itself supports out-of-family prediction, a different estimand, and freezes its design before real memory-loss rho is opened.

biological_question: Does a trait carry a transferable phylogenetic-memory signature across plant families?

interpretation.positive: Knowing the same trait's memory-loss rate in other families improves prediction for a held-out family, implying cross-lineage portability of trait identity.
interpretation.null: Trait identity does not improve out-of-family prediction beyond a training-set global mean on the admitted graph.
interpretation.nonclaim: This does not compare trait variance against family variance and does not imply that lineages are unimportant.

memory_effect.sensitivity: prune-only memory-loss rho on identical core

procedure: For each held-out family f, train on all systems from families other than f.
For each held-out system (f,t), predict rho using the arithmetic mean rho of trait t among training families.
Baseline prediction for every held-out system is the arithmetic mean rho across all training systems.
Pool squared prediction errors over every held-out system exactly once.
portability_statistic.direction: positive values mean trait identity improves cross-lineage prediction
portability_statistic.weighting: one family x trait system = one observation; no family, trait, species-count, or precision weights
portability_statistic.minimum_training_trait_replicates: guaranteed >=4 by final core trait degree >=5 and leave-one-family-out design

permutation_test.null: Within each family independently, permute the observed rho values among that family's fixed trait labels. This preserves each family's response distribution and the exact family-trait incidence graph while destroying cross-family trait correspondence.
permutation_test.rationale: The biological hypothesis is directional: transferable trait identity must reduce prediction error.

prune_only_requirement.rule: Repeat the identical leave-family-out statistic and within-family permutation test using prune-only rho. A robust portability claim requires positive gain and p<=0.05 for both S3 and prune-only.

known_truth_gate.graph: exact 201-edge family-trait incidence, no real rho

benchmark_signal.name: MIXED_TRAIT_SIGNAL
benchmark_signal.provenance: These variance scales are the already-frozen mixed benchmark from the prior model-informativeness design.

benchmark_null.name: TRAIT_NULL_FAMILY_SIGNAL
benchmark_null.rationale: Same total non-residual variance as the signal benchmark, but all repeatable structure is family-specific.

known_truth_gate.failure_rule: If either power or false-positive calibration fails, stop before real rho. Do not change the graph, signal benchmark, statistic, alpha, or permutation structure.

outputs_allowed_after_gate: S3 portability gain and permutation p
prune-only portability gain and permutation p
out-of-family observed/predicted rho pairs at system level
trait-wise training means for descriptive interpretation
